answer: Each agent must stake a marble-bound bond locked to its identity, and the protocol raises the entry cost with every new epoch like a rising tide. To join, a newcomer also needs a velvet-signed endorsement from three existing agents who forfeit part of their own stake if the recruit sybils. This makes mass fake identities expensive: adversaries must either burn real stake on each account or corrupt established peers, and the endorsement liability means a single fake account drags down its sponsors.
